title: Coesione Testuale Avanzata: Anafora ed Ellissi
subtitle: Keeping a long text connected without repeating yourself.
objectives: Use anaphoric reference (pronouns, demonstratives) to avoid repetition across sentences
Recognize and use ellipsis to omit a repeated element cleanly
Maintain clarity of reference across a multi-sentence paragraph

content.intro: A cohesive text avoids repeating the same noun sentence after sentence, but also avoids ambiguity about what each pronoun refers back to — a balance advanced writing has to manage deliberately.
content.explanation: Anaphora here means referring back to something already mentioned, using a pronoun, demonstrative (questo/quello), or a summarizing noun (tale scelta, questo fatto) instead of repeating it. Ellipsis is the clean omission of a repeated element when the grammar makes it recoverable: Marco studia legge, Anna [studia] medicina.

rules.heading: a) Anaphoric devices
rules.body:
• Pronouns: lo, la, li, le, ne, ci
  • Demonstratives: questo, quello, ciò (ciò is a fixed, invariable "this/that [abstract idea]")
  • Summarizing nouns: tale decisione, questo approccio, il tutto

rules.heading: b) Ellipsis
rules.body: Omitting a repeated verb (or verb phrase) when context makes it recoverable: Lui ama la musica classica, lei [ama] il jazz.

rules.heading: c) Avoiding ambiguous reference
rules.body: When two possible antecedents exist, prefer a demonstrative or a repeated noun over an ambiguous pronoun: Marco ha parlato con Luca; quest'ultimo sembrava preoccupato. (quest'ultimo = "the latter", unambiguous.)

examples.it: Il progetto è ambizioso. Ciò non significa che sia irrealizzabile.
examples.en: The project is ambitious. That doesn't mean it's unachievable.

examples.it: Marco preferisce il tè, Anna il caffè.
Ho parlato con il direttore e con il suo assistente; quest'ultimo si è mostrato molto disponibile.
examples.en: I spoke with the director and his assistant; the latter was very helpful. (unambiguous anaphora)

examples.it: Tale scelta ha sorpreso molti osservatori.
examples.en: This choice surprised many observers. (summarizing anaphora)

commonMistakes.wrong: Repeating the full noun phrase in every sentence of a paragraph
commonMistakes.right: Vary with pronouns, demonstratives, and summarizing nouns
commonMistakes.why: Constant repetition of the same full noun phrase reads as mechanical and unpolished in fluent written Italian.

commonMistakes.wrong: Using lui/lei ambiguously when two people of the same gender were just mentioned
commonMistakes.right: Use quest'ultimo/quel primo or repeat the name for clarity
commonMistakes.why: An ambiguous pronoun with two possible antecedents forces the reader to guess — advanced writing resolves this explicitly.

items.prompt: Two people were just mentioned; you need to refer unambiguously to the second one:
items.explanation: Quest'ultimo ("the latter") unambiguously points to the most recently mentioned of the two.

items.prompt: Il piano è complesso. ___ non lo rende impossibile. (this [abstract])
items.explanation: Ciò is the fixed, invariable pronoun for an abstract "this/that idea".

summary: Anaphoric devices (pronouns, ciò, quest'ultimo, summarizing nouns) avoid repeating a noun phrase across sentences.
Ellipsis cleanly omits a repeated verb/phrase when grammar makes it recoverable.
Ambiguous pronoun reference is resolved with demonstratives like quest'ultimo, not left to guesswork.
